allMessages: I’ll inspect the repo’s skill conventions and any existing presentation code, then propose a scope for the evolving diagram, sample presentation, and verification tools.

The repo currently contains only a README and OpenSpec scaffolding, so this change would establish the skill and its scene components.

My recommendation is **go with caveats**: use a shared renderer so generated presentations have consistent navigation and layout, and bound the first version’s project compatibility. I recommend React, TypeScript, and SVG, with a Vite scaffold for projects that lack the components. Vite supports a static browser build, and Playwright can exercise different viewport sizes and capture screenshots. [Vite documentation](https://vite.dev/guide/build), [Playwright documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/emulation).

The proposed scope is:

- An agent skill that turns a topic into a sequence of captioned states of one diagram, preserving element identities as elements appear, move, connect, and change labels.
- Reusable scene components and a player with forward/back navigation, keyboard controls, a focused presenting mode, and a browsing mode with direct step selection.
- Responsive layouts, readable captions, and reduced-motion support.
- Reuse of compatible components where available; otherwise, setup in a dedicated presentation project without replacing the host project’s configuration.
- A sample presentation explaining how to use the skill, authored through the skill itself.
- A reusable verification command that checks the production build, every step, navigation, mode switching, browser errors, and representative desktop, tablet, and phone layouts, producing a report and screenshots.

Automatic checks can catch structural and rendering failures; visual inspection is still needed to judge clarity and explanatory quality. Maintaining the shared renderer and scaffold is the main ongoing cost. A conventional slide tool would reduce that work, but would require adapting the continuous-diagram experience.

I would exclude a visual editor, PowerPoint/PDF export, hosted services, arbitrary framework adapters, and automatic fact-checking. The crosscheck review is skipped as instructed, with no review findings.
